findings.text: The first paragraph says what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. A newcomer can describe the project after reading only that paragraph.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: The header links straight to Next steps. That section lists prerequisites, the clone command, ./setup.sh and a first example command, so the reader knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The first section after the navigation is an error message. It also leaves Athena's main promise unshown: no models, verdict or cost from a real job appear. To a newcomer the page looks broken, and the claim of traceable cost and verdict goes unproven.
findings.source: Check it on a real job — "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The title and most of the page are about firstmate, another project the newcomer has likely never heard of. Someone who came to learn about Athena has to work out that the page is itself a sample of Athena's output. Only the three paragraphs at the top say so.
This header link is for the project owner, not a newcomer. It sits next to the newcomer's next step with no explanation, which may confuse a first-time reader.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision

findings.text: The 'Start here' section opens with seven firstmate terms before it explains anything. That is heavy going for a newcomer who only wants to judge whether Athena is worth trying.
findings.source: Start here — Words used first (captain, yolo, in scope, green, red, local-only landing, home)

findings.text: Claude Code is listed as a prerequisite, but the page never says whether an account or paid API access is needed, or which operating systems are supported. A newcomer may hit those requirements only during setup.
findings.source: Claude Code, or npm to install it.

findings.text: Several glossary entries (captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake) say the source does not define the term. This is honest, and it does show how carefully the study sticks to its sources. But it leaves those terms unexplained for the reader.
findings.source: durable record — "The firstmate source does not define a durable record."
